title: Quasipolynomial dependence on vertices for hypergraph isomorphism
formal: Is there a uniform deterministic algorithm that decides isomorphism of two explicitly represented hypergraphs in time \[2^{C(\log_2(n+2))^{a}}\,N^{b},\] for fixed constants \(C,a,b\geq1\), where \(n\) is the maximum number of underlying vertices and \(N\) is the combined input bit length?
why: This asks whether symmetry testing can depend quasipolynomially only on the underlying universe, while remaining polynomial in the amount of set-system data. It matters for hypergraphs with many large edges and for algorithms that encode structural graph information as set systems.
status_note: The stronger separated-parameter bound is explicitly open in the 2020 source. The source passages were checked on 13 September 2026; a bounded subsequent-work search supplied no verified resolution. Status is source_open.

progress.text: The paper explicitly separates a vertex-dependent exponent on total hypergraph size from the desired fixed polynomial dependence on the number of hyperedges, and leaves the stronger bound open.

importance.reason: A central isomorphism parameter-dependence question for general set systems, with consequences for symmetry algorithms using structural decompositions.

sentences: Hypergraph isomorphism asks whether a relabeling of vertices makes two explicitly listed set systems identical.
The target running time is quasipolynomial in the number of vertices and polynomial in the full input size.
The exponent on input size must be a fixed constant even when many hyperedges are listed.
The source explains why a quasipolynomial bound in the larger incidence representation does not automatically provide this guarantee.
A resolution would extend efficient symmetry testing to rich set systems over comparatively small universes.

definitions: A hypergraph is a finite pair \((V,\mathcal E)\) with \(V=[n]\) and \(\mathcal E\subseteq2^V\). Empty hyperedges and isolated vertices are allowed; edges have no colors, order, weights or repeated copies. The input lists the vertices and every hyperedge explicitly by its incidence bit vector; vertex counts and list lengths are included in the binary encoding. Input length \(N\) therefore includes all incidences and at least \(n\) symbols. An isomorphism from \((V_1,\mathcal E_1)\) to \((V_2,\mathcal E_2)\) is a bijection \(\pi:V_1\to V_2\) with \(\{\pi(e):e\in\mathcal E_1\}=\mathcal E_2\). The algorithm must decide whether one exists and must be correct on every well-formed input; unequal vertex counts imply rejection. Time is worst-case bit time on a deterministic multitape Turing machine with no advice or oracle. Neither the hyperedge size nor the number of hyperedges is bounded polynomially in \(n\). All constants and exponents are uniform over both parameters. Replacing incidence vectors by explicit incidence lists changes length by at most a polynomial and preserves the requested two-parameter bound.

context_blocks.text: The source distinguishes a quasipolynomial dependence on the number of vertices from a polynomial dependence on the possibly much larger collection of hyperedges. Encoding a hypergraph as a bipartite incidence graph does not automatically give that separation of dependencies.

Wiebking discusses a bound whose exponent on total hypergraph size depends polylogarithmically on the vertex count, and explicitly asks for the stronger bound in which the hyperedge-size exponent is constant. The same open question reappears in the outlook section.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of an algorithm with fixed constants satisfying the displayed two-parameter bound, or prove that no such deterministic uniform algorithm exists. A quasipolynomial bound in the full incidence-graph size, or a polynomial exponent depending on the number of vertices or maximum hyperedge size, does not meet the target.

notes: Recovered the precise separated-parameter bound from both occurrences in the primary paper.
